pull_list.title: fix: honor explicit model pick, suppress silent revert on cross-family selection (#3737)
pull_list.body:
## Bug Description

When a user changes the model in the composer dropdown and sends a message, the picker silently snaps back to the profile's default model instead of using the model they just selected. No warning, no toast — the user's choice is silently discarded and the message runs with the reverted model.

Fixes #3737

## Root Cause

`_resolve_compatible_session_model_state` (routes.py:1920) had no way to distinguish an explicit user pick from stale session state. When a bare cross-family model (e.g., `gpt-*` while the profile's provider is `anthropic`) was sent without an explicit `model_provider`, the function compared the model family against the active provider from the catalog, found a mismatch, and rewrote it to the profile default — returning `changed=True` which caused `effective_model` to be emitted.

The client (messages.js:660-665) then **unconditionally** applied `effective_model` to the dropdown, localStorage, and session state — no comparison with the user's original selection, no toast.

Meanwhile, the client already had a pending-model tracking mechanism (`_rememberPendingSessionModel` / `_readPendingSessionModel` in ui.js) that records explicit user picks in sessionStorage with a 10-minute expiry — but it was never consulted during send.

## Fix

**Backend** (api/routes.py):
- Add `explicit_model_pick: bool = False` parameter to `_resolve_compatible_session_model_state`
- When `True`, skip the bare-model cross-provider normalization block (lines 2037-2039) — return the user's model verbatim with `changed=False`
- `_handle_chat_start` extracts `explicit_model_pick` from the POST body and passes it through
- Default `False` ensures all 8 other call sites have unchanged behavior

**Frontend** (static/messages.js):
- Before sending, consult `_readPendingSessionModel(activeSid)` to detect if the outgoing model matches a recent explicit pick
- Include `explicit_model_pick: true` in the POST body when it does
- As defense-in-depth: when `effective_model` is returned and differs from the sent model, show a toast explaining the override instead of silently resetting

## How to Verify

1. Open a session bound to a profile with `model.provider` set (e.g., `anthropic`)
2. In the composer, manually select a **different-family** model (e.g., any `gpt-*` model) without a `@provider:` qualifier
3. Send a message
4. **Expected:** The picker stays on the model you selected. Message runs with your chosen model.
5. If an override still occurs for any reason, a toast appears: "Model changed to X (provider mismatch with active profile)"

## Test Plan

- [x] All 8 existing call sites of `_resolve_compatible_session_model_state` use the default `False` — no behavior change
- [x] `typeof` guards on client-side protect against missing `_readPendingSessionModel`
- [ ] Existing test suite: `tests/test_provider_mismatch.py` — 62 tests exercise model resolution  
- [ ] Existing test suite: `tests/test_issue1855_resolve_model_provider_fast_path.py` — fast-path tests
- [ ] Manual verification with a profile-bound session (cross-family pick)

## Risk Assessment

**Low** — The change is gated behind a new default-false parameter. All existing callers are unaffected. The client-side flag only activates when a pending model match exists (sessionStorage, 10-min window). The toast is a pure addition with no side effects.

Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes a silent model-revert bug where selecting a cross-family model in the composer (e.g., a GPT model under an Anthropic profile) would have the pick overridden by the server without any user-visible feedback. The fix spans a new `explicit_model_pick` backend parameter that short-circuits normalization, client-side detection of the explicit pick via an existing sessionStorage mechanism, and a toast shown when an override still occurs. - **Backend (`api/routes.py`):** `explicit_model_pick: bool = False` is added to `_resolve_compatible_session_model_state`; two early-return guards skip the cross-provider normalization when the flag is `True`. All 8 pre-existing call sites keep the default `False` and are unaffected. - **Frontend (`static/messages.js`):** Before `POST /api/chat/start`, `_readPendingSessionModel` is consulted; the pending pick is matched against the current model *and* provider before the flag is set, and a guarded toast surfaces any remaining server-side override to the user. - **Tests (`tests/test_provider_mismatch.py`):** Two new tests cover the `explicit_model_pick=True` and `=False` variants of the profile-aware normalization path; the parallel catalog-based path added at line 2124 of `routes.py` has no corresponding test yet.

Confidence Score: 3/5

 The fix is gated behind a default-false parameter with no impact on existing call sites, but the profile-aware explicit-pick guard returns `profile_provider` verbatim as the routing provider, meaning a GPT model selected under an Anthropic profile will be routed with `provider="anthropic"` — the exact scenario this PR intends to fix. The provider value returned by the profile-aware guard (line 2023) is `profile_provider` rather than the routing provider inferred from the model's family. For the primary use case — picking `gpt-4o` while a profile's provider is `anthropic` — the backend emits `("gpt-4o", "anthropic", False)`, which flows into `StartRunRequest(provider="anthropic")` and will fail at runtime. The new test fixture pins this same value (`assert provider == "anthropic"`), encoding wrong routing as expected output. Until the guard returns the correct family provider, the core scenario will still error on send. The profile-aware `explicit_model_pick` guard in `api/routes.py` (around line 2023) and its companion test in `tests/test_provider_mismatch.py` need the closest review before merge.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/routes.py | Adds `explicit_model_pick` parameter to `_resolve_compatible_session_model_state`; two early-return guards skip normalization when the flag is `True`. The profile-aware guard returns `profile_provider` unchanged for cross-family models, which previous review comments flagged as incorrect routing. The catalog-based guard at line 2124 has no test coverage. | | static/messages.js | Reads pending session model from sessionStorage before send, compares model + model_provider against current state to detect explicit picks, and includes `explicit_model_pick: true` in the POST body when matched; adds a toast notification guarded on `_explicitPick` when the server overrides the sent model. | | tests/test_provider_mismatch.py | Adds two tests covering the profile-aware `explicit_model_pick` path (True and False). Does not exercise the catalog-based bare-model path (line 2124) that was also modified in this PR. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Picker as Composer Picker (boot.js) participant SS as sessionStorage participant Send as send() (messages.js) participant API as POST /api/chat/start participant Resolve as _resolve_compatible_session_model_state User->>Picker: Select cross-family model (e.g. gpt-4o) Picker->>SS: _rememberPendingSessionModel(sid, model, provider) Picker->>Picker: "S.session.model = gpt-4o" User->>Send: Submit message Send->>SS: _readPendingSessionModel(sid) SS-->>Send: "{model: gpt-4o, model_provider: ...}" Send->>Send: "_explicitPick = (pending.model == state.model && provider match)" Send->>API: "POST {model, model_provider, explicit_model_pick: true}" API->>Resolve: "_resolve_compatible_session_model_state(..., explicit_model_pick=True)" alt profile_provider set, cross-family mismatch (line 2023) Resolve-->>API: (model, profile_provider, False) - wrong provider else no profile, bare model, no slash (line 2124) Resolve-->>API: (model, None, False) else fast path - requested_provider present Resolve-->>API: (model, requested_provider, False) end API-->>Send: "{stream_id, ...}" alt effective_model returned and differs from sent model Send->>User: showToast(Model X changed to Y - profile provider mismatch) end ```
Reviews (3): Last reviewed commit: ["fix: tighten explicit-pick detection and..."](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/commit/5811db68ae53508605dfe98a171c9eef42cce287) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=36022990)

Pulled the branch into a read-only worktree and read the full diff plus `_resolve_compatible_session_model_state` on both your HEAD and `origin/master`. The frontend half is solid, but the backend guard is placed in a branch that won't run for the bug #3737 actually describes — because this branch is based on a commit that predates the regression.

## The frontend half lands cleanly

`_readPendingSessionModel` / `_rememberPendingSessionModel` exist on master (`static/ui.js:1051` and `:1064`, also wired in `static/boot.js:1189,1205`), so consulting the pending pick in `send()` and threading `explicit_model_pick` works. The override toast is a good defense-in-depth addition. No issue there.

## The backend guard is in the wrong branch

Your `merge-base` is `f1211e1f` = **v0.51.267**, but #3448 (the profile-aware resolution that #3737 blames) shipped in **v0.51.290** (commit `47020925`, "fixes #3405"). So your branch's copy of `_resolve_compatible_session_model_state` has *none* of the profile-aware logic. You added the guard here, in the legacy non-profile block:

```python
slash = model.find("/")
if slash < 0:
    if explicit_model_pick:
        # User explicitly chose this model; don't second-guess (#3737)
        return model, requested_provider, False
```

But on current `origin/master`, that legacy `slash < 0` block sits at line ~2117 — *after* the profile-aware branch, which returns first at `api/routes.py:2022-2024`:

```python
if model_family and model_family != _profile_provider_normalized:
    _target = _profile_default or default_model
    return _target, profile_provider, True   # ← the revert #3737 reports
```

For the exact repro in #3737 (bare `gpt-*` pick under an `anthropic`-provider profile), `profile_provider` is truthy and `explicit_provider` is falsy, so master takes the profile branch and returns the swapped model *before execution ever reaches the legacy block where your guard lives*. Once this PR is rebased onto master, the guard becomes dead code for the reported case.

## Two changes needed after rebasing onto master

**1. Move the guard into the profile-aware branch**, before the family-mismatch return at `api/routes.py:2022`:

```python
if profile_provider and not explicit_provider:
    ...
    if explicit_model_pick:
        # Deliberate cross-family pick — honor it, don't repair to profile default (#3737)
        return model, profile_provider, False
    if model_family and model_family != _profile_provider_normalized:
        ...
```

Placing it after the `if not model:` fallback but before the family/slash mismatch returns keeps the empty-model repair intact while sparing a deliberate pick.

**2. Thread the flag through the master call site.** Your `_handle_chat_start` hunk targets line ~11130, but on master it's at `api/routes.py:11359` and the resolve call (~11409) now also passes profile context:

```python
_pp_provider, _pp_default = _read_profile_model_config(s, requested_provider)
model, model_provider, normalized_model = _resolve_compatible_session_model_state(
    requested_model, requested_provider,
    profile_provider=_pp_provider,
    profile_default_model=_pp_default,
    explicit_model_pick=bool(body.get("explicit_model_pick")),
)
```

Expect a merge conflict on this hunk — resolve it by adding the kwarg to the *existing* profile-aware call, not by restoring the older two-arg shape.

## Verification

The existing suites you flagged (`tests/test_provider_mismatch.py`, `tests/test_issue1855_resolve_model_provider_fast_path.py`) won't cover the profile path on their own. Worth adding a case that calls `_resolve_compatible_session_model_state("gpt-5.4-mini", None, profile_provider="anthropic", profile_default_model="claude-...", explicit_model_pick=True)` and asserts it returns `("gpt-5.4-mini", "anthropic", False)` — i.e. the pick survives. Pair it with `explicit_model_pick=False` asserting the existing `changed=True` swap, so the guard's scoping is locked in.

Net: the design is right and matches #3737's suggested shape, but rebase onto current master first, then relocate the guard into the `profile_provider` branch — otherwise the legacy-block placement silently no-ops for the very scenario this fixes.

issue_list.title: [security] Extend symlink-swap TOCTOU hardening to api/routes.py file-API endpoints (raw/zip/editor) + upload cleanup
issue_list.body:
## Summary

A security review of #3398 (workspace symlink-escape containment, shipped v0.51.221) surfaced a **pre-existing** TOCTOU (time-of-check-to-time-of-use) class affecting the **`api/routes.py` file-API endpoints** that #3398 did not touch. These endpoints validate a path with `api.helpers.safe_resolve()` and then re-open / read / write / delete by **pathname**, so a path component swapped to an external symlink *between* validation and use can escape the workspace.

This is the same race class #3398 closed for the *workspace-tree* read/list/upload/extract paths (via the new portable anchored `openat`-walk helpers `open_anchored_fd` / `open_anchored_create_fd` / `make_anchored_dir` in `api/workspace.py`). This issue tracks extending that hardening to the remaining `routes.py` file-API surface.

## Why it was scoped separately from #3398

- #3398's diff is confined to `api/workspace.py` + `api/upload.py` (+ tests). It never modified `api/routes.py`.
- These endpoints use a **different** validator (`api.helpers.safe_resolve`), not the `api.workspace.safe_resolve_ws` that #3398 hardened.
- The race is **pre-existing in master** — it predates #3398 and was not introduced or widened by it. #3398 is a net security improvement (it closes the no-race static symlink-escape exfil path and the workspace-tree TOCTOU); this is the remaining, lower-likelihood surface.

## Threat model / likelihood

TOCTOU here requires an attacker to win a sub-millisecond swap race against the server's own file API. The **higher-likelihood, no-race** exfiltration path (an in-workspace symlink to `~/.ssh` / `~/.hermes/auth.json` read through `/api/list` / `read_file_content`) is **already closed** by #3398. This issue is the race-only residue on the broader endpoint set.

## Endpoints to harden (from the review)

1. **`/api/file/raw`** (`routes.py` ~8277) + inline HTML preview (`_serve_inline_html_preview`, ~8494) — validates via `_file_raw_target()` then `target.open("rb")` / `target.read_bytes()` by pathname. Fix: read through `open_anchored_fd(Path(s.workspace), target, want_dir=False)` and stream/read from the fd.
2. **Folder download zip** (`routes.py` ~9033) — preflights paths then `ZipFile.write(path)` reopens each by pathname. Fix: store workspace-relative paths during collection, reopen each via `open_anchored_fd()` immediately before writing, write via `ZipInfo`/`zf.open()` from the verified fd.
3. **File-editor endpoints** (`routes.py` ~11437): write/create (`target.write_text()`), mkdir (`target.mkdir()`), delete (`target.unlink()` / `shutil.rmtree()`), rename (`source.rename(dest)`) — all pathname ops after `safe_resolve()`. Fix: create → `open_anchored_create_fd`; mkdir → `make_anchored_dir`; save → a new anchored `O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC|O_NOFOLLOW` helper; delete/rename → anchored `unlinkat`/`renameat`-style helpers (or refuse when they can't be done without following pathnames).
4. **Archive upload/extraction cleanup** (`upload.py` ~313 `shutil.rmtree(dest_dir)` on failure, ~499 archive unlink) — pathname cleanup after anchored create. Fix: anchored recursive cleanup under the workspace, or skip auto-cleanup when it can't be done without following pathnames.

## Building blocks already in place (from #3398, v0.51.221)

`api/workspace.py` now has the portable anchored primitives to build on (Linux/macOS via `openat`+`dir_fd`, Windows path-based fallback gated on `os.supports_dir_fd`):
- `open_anchored_fd(root, target, *, want_dir)` — race-safe read/list open.
- `open_anchored_create_fd(root, dest)` — race-safe `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` create.
- `make_anchored_dir(root, dest)` — race-safe anchored mkdir walk.

This issue needs two more siblings: an anchored **truncate-open** (for editor save/overwrite) and anchored **unlink/rename** helpers.

## Acceptance

- All four endpoint groups read/write/delete/rename through anchored fd helpers (no pathname op after the containment check).
- Regression tests with the validate-then-symlink-swap pattern (mirroring `tests/test_workspace_symlink_containment.py`'s TOCTOU tests) for each endpoint.
- Windows/no-`dir_fd` fallback preserved (no bricking — same pattern as #3398's `list_dir` split).

_Filed from the #3398 review (Codex round-4 findings). Severity: medium (race-only; the no-race exfil path is already closed)._

pull_list.title: [security] fix(git): anchor discard untracked deletes
pull_list.body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the Git workspace discard boundary for untracked-file deletion.

- Fixes a validation-to-use symlink-swap window in `git_discard(..., delete_untracked=True)`.
- Reuses the existing workspace anchored deletion helpers instead of adding a separate Git-specific guard.
- Preserves the prior `missing_ok=True` behavior for benign races where an untracked file disappears before unlink.
- Adds regression coverage showing both the symlink-swap block and the concurrent-missing-file tolerance.
- This is a sibling hardening area to prior workspace symlink-containment work, but the affected code path here is `api/workspace_git.py` Git discard cleanup.

## Security issues covered

| Issue | Impact | Severity |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Git discard untracked-delete symlink race | A workspace-controlled path component can be swapped after validation so an untracked-file discard attempts to delete an outside path | Medium |

## Before this PR

- `git_discard()` resolved and validated the requested workspace path with `safe_resolve_ws()`.
- The untracked-delete branch then deleted through the resolved pathname with `Path.unlink()` or `shutil.rmtree()`.
- That left a race window between containment validation and filesystem use.
- There was no regression test proving Git discard untracked-delete stayed anchored at the workspace boundary under a symlink swap.

## After this PR

- Untracked-file deletion uses `unlink_anchored(ctx.workspace, target)` while still tolerating `FileNotFoundError` for benign concurrent removal.
- Untracked-directory deletion uses `rmtree_anchored(ctx.workspace, target)`.
- The final delete operation now shares the existing workspace anchored boundary instead of trusting only the earlier resolved pathname.
- A regression test simulates the validation-to-use race and locks in the blocked behavior.

## Why this matters

Hermes WebUI can expose workspace operations through the browser. A discard operation that deletes untracked paths should only affect files inside the configured workspace, even if another process can modify that workspace concurrently.

Before this fix, a local workspace writer could replace a validated path component with a symlink before the direct pathname delete occurred. In that race, Git discard cleanup could target a file outside the workspace boundary.

## How this differs from related issue/PR

I found related prior hardening work in #3450 for `api/routes.py` file-API endpoints.

This PR covers a different surface:

- component: `api/workspace_git.py`
- trigger: `git_discard(..., delete_untracked=True)`
- unsafe operation: direct pathname delete after workspace validation
- fix pattern: reuse existing anchored delete helpers for the Git discard cleanup path

The earlier route-file hardening does not cover this Git discard untracked-delete branch, so this small follow-up is still needed.

## Attack flow

```text
Workspace writer can modify path components during discard
    -> WebUI Git discard deletes an untracked path
        -> path is validated with safe_resolve_ws()
            -> path component is swapped to a symlink before direct pathname deletion
                -> delete can affect an outside file instead of staying inside the workspace
```

## Affected code

| Issue | Files |
|-------|-------|
| Git discard untracked-delete symlink race | `api/workspace_git.py`, `tests/test_workspace_git.py` |

## Root cause

Issue: Git discard untracked-delete symlink race

- The code correctly performed a workspace containment check before deletion.
- The final deletion still used the normal pathname APIs, so it could observe a different filesystem graph than the one validated earlier.
- The Git discard path did not reuse the existing anchored workspace deletion helpers, creating a sibling boundary that could drift from the rest of the workspace hardening.

## CVSS assessment

| Issue | CVSS v3.1 | Vector |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Git discard untracked-delete symlink race | 5.0 Medium | `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:N/I:L/A:H` |

Rationale:

- The attacker condition is local/workspace-adjacent: the attacker needs the ability to modify the workspace path during the discard operation.
- Exploitation also requires winning a race, so attack complexity is high.
- The impact is bounded to filesystem effects reachable through the raced delete path; the proof demonstrates outside-file deletion rather than code execution or secret disclosure.

## Safe reproduction steps

The issue was reproduced locally with a temporary workspace proof, without production paths or secrets:

1. Create a temporary Git repo workspace.
2. Create an untracked workspace file at `repo/d/f`.
3. Create an outside victim file at `outside/f`.
4. Patch `api.workspace_git.safe_resolve_ws` in the proof harness so that after `git_discard()` performs its second validation for `d/f`, the harness replaces `repo/d` with a symlink to `outside`.
5. Call the real `git_discard(repo, ["d/f"], delete_untracked=True)`.
6. Observe the pre-patch behavior deletes the outside victim file.

## Expected vulnerable behavior

Pre-patch proof signal:

```text
RESULT=OUTSIDE_FILE_DELETED
```

That signal means the untracked discard operation deleted the outside victim file after the path component was swapped between validation and use.

After this PR, the same raced path is blocked by the anchored helper:

```text
ValueError: Path traversal blocked
```

The regression test also asserts the outside victim file still exists and its contents are unchanged.

## Changes in this PR

- Imports `unlink_anchored` and `rmtree_anchored` from `api.workspace`.
- Replaces direct untracked-file deletion with `unlink_anchored(ctx.workspace, target)`.
- Replaces direct untracked-directory deletion with `rmtree_anchored(ctx.workspace, target)`.
- Removes the now-unused `shutil` import from `api/workspace_git.py`.
- Adds a regression test for the symlink-swap validation-to-use race in Git discard cleanup.
- Adds a regression test for the `missing_ok=True` compatibility path when an untracked file disappears concurrently.

## Files changed

| Category | Files | What changed |
|----------|-------|--------------|
| Security fix | `api/workspace_git.py` | Reused anchored delete helpers for untracked Git discard cleanup |
| Tests | `tests/test_workspace_git.py` | Added race regression tests for outside-victim preservation and concurrent missing-file tolerance |

## Maintainer impact

- The patch is intentionally small and limited to untracked cleanup inside `git_discard()`; it keeps the previous benign missing-file behavior for ordinary concurrent-delete races.
- Tracked-file discard still delegates to `git restore`.
- No frontend, API schema, dependency, or public workflow changes are included.
- Reusing the existing workspace anchored helpers keeps this boundary aligned with the rest of the path-containment hardening and reduces future drift.

## Fix rationale

The security boundary being enforced is the configured workspace root. That boundary should hold at the point of deletion, not only at an earlier validation step.

Using the existing anchored helpers is the narrowest durable fix because those helpers already encode the repository's intended symlink-containment behavior for workspace deletes. The new test then exercises the specific Git discard branch that previously bypassed that final anchored operation.

## Type of change

- [x] Security fix
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor with no behavior change

## Test plan

- [x] Git discard regression test for the symlink-swap race.
- [x] Git discard regression test for concurrent untracked-file disappearance.
- [x] Existing workspace symlink containment tests.

Executed with:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_workspace_git.py tests/test_workspace_symlink_containment.py -q
```

Result:

```text
Running 50 items in this shard
.............................................s....                       [100%]
49 passed, 1 skipped, 1 warning in 11.91s
```

## Disclosure notes

- This PR is based on local code review and a safe temporary-workspace reproduction.
- No production systems, real user workspaces, or secrets were used.
- No unrelated files were changed.
- The patch intentionally shares the existing workspace anchored delete boundary instead of adding a parallel Git-specific implementation.

pull_list.title: feat(config): expand ${VAR} references in config.yaml at load time
pull_list.body:
## Problem

`config.yaml` already supports `${ENV_VAR}` substitution in **hermes-agent** (via `_expand_env_vars` in `hermes_cli/config.py`). However, the WebUI's own config loader (`api/config.py`) called `yaml.safe_load()` and stored the raw dict directly — leaving literal `${...}` strings in place.

This caused a silent but painful failure: users who placed credentials in their profile `.env` (e.g. `NEWAPI_BASE_URL=http://10.x.x.x/v1`) and referenced them via `${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}` in `config.yaml` would see the agent fail immediately with:

```
🌐 Endpoint: ${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}
📝 Error: Connection error.
```

The unexpanded string was being passed as the OpenAI client's `base_url`, making every API call fail with a connection error, even though the `.env` file was correctly populated.

## Fix

Add a small recursive `_expand_env_vars()` helper that mirrors the one already in `hermes_cli/config.py`:

```python
def _expand_env_vars(obj):
    """Recursively expand ${VAR} references in config values using os.environ."""
    if isinstance(obj, str):
        return re.sub(r"\${([^}]+)}", lambda m: os.environ.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)), obj)
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: _expand_env_vars(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        return [_expand_env_vars(item) for item in obj]
    return obj
```

Apply it in both config load paths:
- `reload_config()` — the main cached loader triggered on profile switch and file mtime change
- `_load_yaml_config_file()` — the per-profile-home loader used by worker threads for non-default profiles

Unresolved references (variable not set in `os.environ`) are left verbatim, matching hermes-agent's existing behaviour.

## Notes

- `re` and `os` are already imported in `api/config.py` — no new dependencies introduced
- 14 lines added, 2 lines changed; fully backward-compatible (no-op when no `${...}` references are present)

## Test plan

- [ ] Place `NEWAPI_BASE_URL=http://your-endpoint/v1` in `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/.env`
- [ ] Reference it as `base_url: ${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}` in `profiles/<name>/config.yaml`
- [ ] Start a chat session in the WebUI under that profile — agent should connect successfully (no `Endpoint: ${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}` error)
- [ ] Profiles with no `${...}` references in config continue to work unchanged

---

最后，真诚地感谢 @nesquena 对 hermes-webui 项目的持续投入与无私奉献。这个项目架构清晰、文档完整、代码质量极高，是一个非常值得学习的开源项目。能在这样用心维护的代码库上做贡献，感到非常荣幸。感谢你愿意花时间和精力打磨这个工具，并慷慨地分享给整个社区！🙏

The expanded dict is immediately written back to disk by `_save_yaml_config_file`, permanently replacing `${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}` (and all other `${...}` references) with their resolved strings after the first WebUI write operation.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The fix correctly expands env vars for the in-memory config cache used at runtime, but `_load_yaml_config_file` is also used as the read side of read-modify-write cycles (model selection, reasoning settings, skill toggles, MCP server mutations). After expansion there, `_save_yaml_config_file` bakes the resolved URLs and other values directly into `config.yaml`, permanently erasing the `${...}` references the user set up. The feature would work once, then silently stop working after any WebUI write operation. api/config.py — specifically the `_load_yaml_config_file` change and every caller that follows a read-modify-write pattern with `_save_yaml_config_file`.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/config.py | Adds `_expand_env_vars()` helper and applies it in `reload_config()` and `_load_yaml_config_file()`. The `reload_config()` application (for the in-memory cache) is correct, but expanding in `_load_yaml_config_file()` silently bakes resolved env-var values into disk writes wherever that function is used in a read-modify-write cycle. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant WebUI participant config_py as api/config.py participant disk as config.yaml Note over config_py,disk: Runtime read path (correct) WebUI->>config_py: get_config() config_py->>disk: read config.yaml config_py->>config_py: _expand_env_vars() resolves placeholders config_py-->>WebUI: expanded _cfg_cache Note over config_py,disk: Read-modify-write path (broken) User->>WebUI: Toggle MCP server / change model WebUI->>config_py: _load_yaml_config_file(config_path) config_py->>disk: read config.yaml config_py->>config_py: _expand_env_vars() resolves placeholders config_py-->>WebUI: expanded dict with refs lost WebUI->>config_py: _save_yaml_config_file(path, expanded_dict) config_py->>disk: write — placeholders permanently replaced ```
Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["feat(config): expand \\${VAR} references ..."](https://github.com/nesquena/hermes-webui/commit/e07377921a98d9edbef4db80651944e3a9920d1c) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=36017131)

Pulled the branch into a read-only worktree and read both hunks against `origin/master`, plus the agent's `_expand_env_vars` in `hermes_cli/config.py`. The gap is real and the helper itself is a faithful port — but applying it inside `_load_yaml_config_file` will silently clobber `${VAR}` templates on the Settings save paths. That needs scoping before merge.

## The gap is genuine and the helper matches the contract

You're right that `api/config.py` read `config.yaml` raw while the agent expanded it. Your helper is byte-identical to the agent's at `hermes_cli/config.py:4829-4845` — same regex `\${([^}]+)}`, same `os.environ.get(name, original)` verbatim-on-miss fallback. So the expansion semantics are correct.

## Blocking issue: `_load_yaml_config_file` is also the read side of read-modify-write saves

`_load_yaml_config_file` isn't only consumed for reading — several Settings mutators use it as the *read* half of a read-modify-write against the same file, then re-dump the **entire** dict via `_save_yaml_config_file` (which is a plain `yaml.safe_dump(config_data)`, no template preservation):

- `set_reasoning_display` — `api/config.py:2531`
- `set_reasoning_effort` — `api/config.py:2559`
- `set_hermes_default_model` — `api/config.py:2581`
- `set_auxiliary_model` — `api/config.py:2702`

Each does:

```python
with _cfg_lock:
    config_data = _load_yaml_config_file(config_path)   # ← now returns EXPANDED dict
    model_cfg = config_data.get("model", {})
    ...
    _save_yaml_config_file(config_path, config_data)     # ← dumps expanded value back
```

With your change, a user who toggles *any* unrelated setting (say reasoning effort) while their `config.yaml` has `base_url: ${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}` gets that template resolved to the literal endpoint and written back to disk — because the whole dict is re-serialized, not just the key they touched. The `${VAR}` reference is destroyed permanently, and worse, a resolved secret can land in `config.yaml` in plaintext. This is exactly the regression the issue you're fixing was trying to avoid.

## How the agent avoids it — and what's missing here

The agent doesn't expand-then-save. Its `save_config` (`hermes_cli/config.py:5233-5273`) re-reads the *raw* (unexpanded) file and runs `_preserve_env_ref_templates` to keep `${VAR}` templates whenever the rendered value still matches the env expansion:

```python
raw_existing = _normalize_root_model_keys(_normalize_max_turns_config(read_raw_config()))
if raw_existing:
    normalized = _preserve_env_ref_templates(
        normalized, raw_existing,
        _LAST_EXPANDED_CONFIG_BY_PATH.get(str(config_path)),
    )
```

The WebUI has no equivalent of `_preserve_env_ref_templates` or the `_LAST_EXPANDED_CONFIG_BY_PATH` bookkeeping, so it can't do that reconciliation.

## Recommended scoping

The cleanest minimal fix is to keep expansion off the shared loader and apply it only on the read-only consumption paths. Add a flag rather than expanding unconditionally:

```python
def _load_yaml_config_file(config_path: Path, *, expand: bool = False) -> dict:
    ...
    loaded = _yaml.safe_load(...)
    if not isinstance(loaded, dict):
        return {}
    return _expand_env_vars(loaded) if expand else loaded
```

Then pass `expand=True` only where the result is consumed (your `reload_config()` cache update, and `get_config_for_profile_home`/`streaming.py:5415` worker reads), and leave the four `set_*` save callers reading raw so their re-dump preserves the templates. That fixes the original `Endpoint: ${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}` failure (runtime consumers see the expanded value) without the clobber.

## Test plan additions

Beyond the round-trip you listed, please add: set `base_url: ${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}` in `config.yaml`, then call `set_reasoning_effort("high")` via Settings, and assert `config.yaml` on disk still contains the literal `${NEWAPI_BASE_URL}` (not the resolved endpoint). That's the regression this scoping prevents, and it's worth a unit test so it can't silently come back.

One small note for the description: the env vars come from the profile `.env` loaded into `os.environ` by `_reload_dotenv` (`api/profiles.py:812`) on profile switch / `profile_env_for_background_worker` for workers — so expansion correctly sees them on the request and streaming threads, but only because that load already ran. Worth keeping in mind if you add expansion anywhere that runs before the profile env is applied.

## Release v0.51.303 — Release JS (stage-p1a)

Three low-risk contributor fixes, each rebased onto fresh master (original branches were 9 commits stale — revert-guard would have rolled back releases on a direct squash). Rebase fidelity verified byte-identical to each PR head; dependencies confirmed present on master.

### Fixed
- **#3732** (@mysoul12138) — cron run output rows were expand-only; clicking an open row re-fetched pointlessly. Now toggles (collapse + clear state + early return).

### Security
- **#3702** (@Hinotoi-agent) — `git_discard(delete_untracked=true)` now deletes untracked files via the anchored helpers (`rmtree_anchored`/`unlink_anchored`), closing a validation-to-use symlink-swap window; preserves missing_ok tolerance. Regression tests for both the swap-block and concurrent-missing-file cases.

### Gates
- Full suite: **8120 passed**, 0 failed (one prior run hit the boot-cascade flake — 448× connection-refused, 0 code errors — cleared on clean re-run)
- Codex regression gate: **SAFE TO SHIP** (ran #3702's tests directly: 2 passed)
- Opus correctness gate: **SAFE TO SHIP**

- Revert-guard: origin/master is ancestor

Closes #3732, closes #3736, closes #3702.

feat(config): expand ${VAR} references in config.yaml at load time (#3736)

hermes-agent already expands ${ENV_VAR} in config.yaml, but the WebUI's own

Co-authored-by: Carry00 <Carry00@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(security): anchor untracked-file deletes in git_discard (#3702)

git_discard(delete_untracked=True) used raw shutil.rmtree / Path.unlink after a
separate safe_resolve_ws validation, leaving a validation-to-use symlink-swap
window. Route untracked deletes through the anchored helpers (rmtree_anchored /
unlink_anchored) so a swapped path component is rejected at delete time; preserve
the prior missing_ok tolerance for benign concurrent-removal races. Adds
regression coverage for both the symlink-swap block and the concurrent-missing case.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The env-var expansion in config.py is applied to both load paths consistently. The JS toggle is a straightforward branch inversion. description: Hermes WebUI before version 0.51.303 contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability in the git_discard function within api/workspace_git.py that allows attackers to delete files outside the configured workspace boundary by replacing a validated path component with a symlink after validation but before deletion. Attackers can substitute a workspace-controlled path component with a symlink pointing to an external directory between the safe_resolve_ws() validation step and the subsequent Path.unlink() or shutil.rmtree() deletion call, causing the delete operation to follow the symlink and remove arbitrary files outside the workspace.

pull_list.title: [security] harden workspace Git config execution
pull_list.body:
## Summary
This PR hardens workspace Git operations so a repository's local Git configuration cannot turn WebUI status/fetch calls into host command execution.

- Blocks a validated read-only `git status` issue where repo-local `core.fsmonitor` executed an arbitrary helper during workspace status refresh.
- Blocks a validated default-enabled `git fetch --prune` issue where repo-local transport/SSH/authentication configuration could execute an arbitrary helper from `.git/config`.
- Adds regression tests that set malicious repo-local config and assert the helper marker is not created.
- Sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so disabled credential helpers fail fast instead of hanging on an interactive prompt.

## Security issues covered

| Issue | Impact | Severity |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Read-only workspace Git status honors repo-local `core.fsmonitor` | A malicious/restored workspace repository can execute a local helper when the UI/API asks for status, even though the operation is presented as read-only. | High |
| Default-enabled workspace Git fetch honors repo-local executable transport/auth config | A malicious/restored workspace repository can execute a local helper when `/api/git/fetch` invokes `git fetch --prune`, without requiring destructive workspace Git mode. | High |

## Before this PR
- `_run_git()` scrubbed selected inherited Git environment variables but still invoked `git` in a way that honored repo-local executable config.
- `git_status()` could execute `core.fsmonitor` from `.git/config` during a read-only status refresh.
- `git_fetch()` could execute repo-local fetch-related config such as an enabled `ext::` transport helper, `core.sshCommand`, `core.askPass`, or `credential.helper`.
- Regression coverage checked environment scrubbing, but not repo-local Git configuration that Git itself loads after process startup.

## After this PR
- All workspace Git subprocesses are invoked with hardened command-line config:
  - `core.fsmonitor=false`
  - `core.sshCommand=ssh`
  - `core.askPass=`
  - `credential.helper=`
  - `protocol.ext.allow=never`
- Inherited `GIT_ASKPASS`, `SSH_ASKPASS`, `GIT_SSH`, and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` are scrubbed alongside the existing Git config environment variables.
- `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is forced for workspace Git subprocesses so HTTPS auth failures fail fast rather than waiting for a terminal prompt.
- New tests cover validated executable config classes:
  - status ignores a malicious repo-local `core.fsmonitor` helper
  - fetch refuses a repo-local `ext::` transport helper even when the repo config enables it
  - fetch ignores repo-local `credential.helper` and `core.askPass` helpers
  - environment hardening preserves `GIT_INDEX_FILE` while forcing `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`

## Why this matters
```text
attacker-controlled or restored workspace repository
    -> workspace Git status/fetch API path
        -> Git loads repo-local .git/config
            -> executable Git config runs a helper command
                -> host command execution in the WebUI process environment
```

The affected calls are especially sensitive because status is read-only and fetch is allowed without `HERMES_WEBUI_WORKSPACE_GIT_DESTRUCTIVE=1`, so operators may not expect them to execute repository-provided helpers.

## Affected code

| Issue | Files |
|-------|-------|
| Repo-local Git config execution from status/fetch | `api/workspace_git.py` |
| Regression coverage | `tests/test_workspace_git.py` |
| Behavior documentation and changelog note | `docs/workspace-git.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` |

## Root cause
Issue 1: read-only Git status executes `core.fsmonitor`
- `git status` honors `core.fsmonitor` from repo-local Git config.
- The workspace Git wrapper did not override that config before running status-oriented commands.

Issue 2: default-enabled Git fetch executes repo-local transport/auth config
- `git fetch --prune` honors remote URL/protocol and authentication helper configuration stored in repo-local Git config.
- `/api/git/fetch` is intentionally not gated as destructive, but the underlying Git invocation still allowed executable transport/authentication configuration.

## CVSS assessment

| Issue | CVSS v3.1 | Vector |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Read-only status / `core.fsmonitor` execution | 8.0 High | `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N` |
| Default-enabled fetch / executable transport/auth config | 8.0 High | `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N` |

Rationale: the attacker must already be able to influence the workspace repository or restored session state, but once that condition is met, a read/status/fetch action can execute code in the WebUI host context. Scope is changed because repository content/config crosses into host process execution.

## Safe reproduction steps
### 1. Read-only `core.fsmonitor` execution
1. Create a workspace repository with a repo-local `core.fsmonitor` command that writes a marker file.
2. Call the workspace Git status helper/API.
3. Vulnerable behavior: the marker file is created during a read-only status operation.
4. Patched behavior: status completes and the marker file is not created.

### 2. Fetch transport helper execution
1. Create a workspace repository with `protocol.ext.allow=always` and an `origin` URL using an `ext::` helper that writes a marker file.
2. Call the workspace Git fetch helper/API.
3. Vulnerable behavior: Git invokes the helper and creates the marker file.
4. Patched behavior: fetch fails as a Git error and the marker file is not created.

### 3. Fetch authentication helper execution
1. Create a workspace repository with an HTTPS remote that returns 401 and repo-local `credential.helper` or `core.askPass` pointing to a marker-writing helper.
2. Call the workspace Git fetch helper/API.
3. Vulnerable behavior: Git may invoke the helper during authentication.
4. Patched behavior: fetch fails as an auth error, no helper marker is created, and Git cannot block on a terminal prompt.

## Changes in this PR
- Adds `_GIT_HARDENED_CONFIG` and `_hardened_git_argv()` so workspace Git commands consistently pass safe command-line config to Git.
- Overrides repo-local `core.fsmonitor`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.askPass`, `credential.helper`, and `protocol.ext.allow` for workspace Git subprocesses.
- Scrubs inherited `GIT_ASKPASS`, `SSH_ASKPASS`, `GIT_SSH`, and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` from the Git subprocess environment.
- Forces `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for workspace Git subprocesses.
- Adds regression tests for repo-local config execution paths and environment hardening.
- Documents the HTTPS credential-helper behavior change in `docs/workspace-git.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Adds `strict=True` to nearby `zip()` calls so the touched file passes the existing ruff gate.

## Maintainer impact
- Patch scope is limited to workspace Git subprocess invocation, workspace Git docs/changelog, and tests.
- Frontend, sessions, model providers, uploads, and unrelated API routes are untouched.
- SSH fetches use the normal `ssh` binary instead of allowing repo-local `core.sshCommand` overrides; `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is not scrubbed, so ssh-agent based remotes continue to work.
- `ext::` transports, repo-local askpass commands, and repo-local credential helpers remain blocked for workspace Git operations, which is the safe default for untrusted/restored workspaces.
- Private HTTPS remotes that rely on a stored credential helper may need to use an SSH remote or another externally authenticated transport from WebUI.

## Fix rationale
- Command-line `git -c` config has higher precedence than repo-local config, making it a narrow and durable place to enforce this boundary.
- Keeping the hardening inside `_run_git()` protects all workspace Git callers consistently, including future status/diff/fetch wrappers.
- Forcing `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` prevents auth failures from holding the remote-operation lock until timeout.
- The regression tests assert the important security property directly: malicious helper marker files are not created.

## Type of change
- [x] Security fix
- [x] Tests
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor with no behavior change

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/test_workspace_git.py -q`
- [x] `python -m ruff check api/workspace_git.py tests/test_workspace_git.py`
- [ ] Full project test suite was not run; this PR changes only workspace Git subprocess hardening/docs and the targeted workspace Git test module was run.

## Disclosure notes
- No production systems were tested.
- The reproduction payloads use local marker files only; no secrets or external targets are required.
- No unrelated application areas were changed.

Greptile Summary

 This PR hardens all workspace Git subprocess calls against arbitrary code execution via attacker-controlled `.git/config`, patching two validated High-severity vectors (read-only `core.fsmonitor` execution and default-enabled `git fetch` ext-transport execution) along with the previously identified `credential.helper` and `core.askPass` gaps. - Adds `_GIT_HARDENED_CONFIG` (five `-c` key=value pairs) applied via `_hardened_git_argv()` to every `_run_git()` call, overriding `core.fsmonitor`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.askPass`, `credential.helper`, and `protocol.ext.allow` before Git loads repo-local config. - Scrubs `GIT_ASKPASS`, `SSH_ASKPASS`, `GIT_SSH`, and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` from the subprocess environment and sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` to prevent interactive credential prompts. - Adds four regression tests that assert malicious helper marker files are not created for each covered attack class.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 Safe to merge after addressing the remaining core.gitProxy code-execution path in _GIT_HARDENED_CONFIG. The hardening is well-structured and tests directly verify that malicious helper marker files are not created. One remaining gap: repo-local core.gitProxy is not overridden, so a workspace .git/config that pairs a git:// remote URL with a core.gitProxy command will still execute that command during git fetch. The attacker who can write .git/config controls the remote URL too, making this equally reachable as the ext:: and fsmonitor vectors that were explicitly patched. api/workspace_git.py — specifically the _GIT_HARDENED_CONFIG tuple, which needs a core.gitProxy entry to close the remaining execution path.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/workspace_git.py | Adds _GIT_HARDENED_CONFIG and _hardened_git_argv() to prepend safety -c overrides to every workspace Git call; also scrubs GIT_ASKPASS, SSH_ASKPASS, GIT_SSH, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, and sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. One code-execution path remains: repo-local core.gitProxy can still run an arbitrary command for git:// remotes. | | tests/test_workspace_git.py | Adds four regression tests that directly assert malicious marker files are not created: core.fsmonitor helper, ext:: transport, repo-local credential.helper, and repo-local core.askPass. Tests use a real in-process HTTP 401 server to validate credential/askpass blocking without mocking the hardened argv. | | docs/workspace-git.md | Updated to document the new environment scrubbing (GIT_ASKPASS, SSH_ASKPASS, GIT_SSH, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0) and the operator note that HTTPS remotes requiring credential helpers will fail. | | CHANGELOG.md | Adds a Security section under Unreleased with an accurate high-level summary of the hardening applied to workspace Git operations. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Browser participant WebUI as WebUI API participant RunGit as _run_git participant Git as git subprocess participant Repo as .git/config Browser->>WebUI: GET /api/git/status or POST /api/git/fetch WebUI->>RunGit: git_status or git_fetch Note over RunGit: _hardened_git_argv prepends -c overrides Note over RunGit: _clean_git_env scrubs GIT_ASKPASS SSH_ASKPASS GIT_SSH GIT_SSH_COMMAND and sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 RunGit->>Git: "git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.sshCommand=ssh -c core.askPass= -c credential.helper= -c protocol.ext.allow=never" Git->>Repo: load .git/config Note over Git,Repo: -c flags override repo-local config, malicious helpers are never invoked Git-->>RunGit: exit code and output RunGit-->>WebUI: CompletedProcess WebUI-->>Browser: JSON response ```

events.message: Block workspace Git askpass helpers

events.body:
Reviewed read-only against `origin/master`: the diff for `api/workspace_git.py`, the full file at HEAD, and the four new regression tests in `tests/test_workspace_git.py`. CI is green across all 11 checks. The centralization approach is the right one — this is a solid hardening PR. Three notes, one functional, before merge.

## Centralization is complete — no bypass

Every workspace Git call routes through `_run_git`, and `_run_git` is the sole `subprocess.run` site. The `-c` overrides are injected there:

```python
# api/workspace_git.py:164-165
result = subprocess.run(
    _hardened_git_argv(args),
```

I grepped all ~40 `_run_git(` call sites (status, fetch, pull, push, stash, switch, commit, restore, read-tree, …) and none construct a bare `["git", …]` argv of their own. So `core.fsmonitor`, `protocol.ext.allow`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.askPass`, and `credential.helper` are enforced uniformly, including the read-only `git_status()` and the un-gated `git_fetch()`. Good — this is durable against future wrappers.

## HEAD does more than the PR body says

The PR description's "After this PR" list and the affected-code table mention `core.fsmonitor`, `core.sshCommand`, `protocol.ext.allow`, and `GIT_SSH`/`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`. But `53aec827` also adds `core.askPass=""`, `credential.helper=""`, and scrubs `GIT_ASKPASS`/`SSH_ASKPASS`:

```python
# api/workspace_git.py:46-52
_GIT_HARDENED_CONFIG = (
    ("core.fsmonitor", "false"),
    ("core.sshCommand", "ssh"),
    ("core.askPass", ""),
    ("credential.helper", ""),
    ("protocol.ext.allow", "never"),
)
```

That's a fine expansion (it closes the askpass/credential-helper execution classes the 4th test exercises), but the PR body and table should be updated to match so a reviewer signing off on "five overrides" knows that's intentional.

## GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT — endorse the gap, but the fix is *set*, not scrub

Greptile's liveness note is correct and worth acting on. With `credential.helper` and `core.askPass` both disabled, a fetch/pull against a private HTTPS remote that 401s has no non-interactive way to get credentials. Without `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, Git may fall back to prompting on the controlling terminal and block until `GIT_REMOTE_TIMEOUT` (60s, `workspace_git.py:24`) expires — holding the mutation lock the whole time.

The important subtlety: adding `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` to `_GIT_ENV_SCRUB_KEYS` is **not** enough — scrubbing only removes an inherited value, leaving Git's default (prompt-if-tty). You want to *force* non-interactive by setting it in `_clean_git_env`:

```python
env = os.environ.copy()
...
env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"   # fail fast instead of blocking on a prompt
```

That converts the 60s hang into an immediate auth failure.

## Functional trade-off worth a CHANGELOG/docs line

`credential.helper=""` means legitimate private **HTTPS** remotes that rely on a stored credential helper will now fail on `git_fetch`/`git_pull`/`git_push` (1262/1271/1288), not just attacker repos. SSH remotes are unaffected — `core.sshCommand=ssh` keeps the default binary and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` isn't scrubbed, so ssh-agent/keys still resolve. For untrusted/restored workspaces this is the correct default, but it's a real behavior change for users pushing to private HTTPS origins. A one-line note in the PR/CHANGELOG ("workspace HTTPS pushes now require an SSH remote or an externally-authenticated transport") would save a confused bug report.

## Verdict

Mechanically sound, no auth/routing/data-model paths touched, tests assert the security property directly (no marker file). I'd ask for the `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` set and the body/CHANGELOG sync before merge; the credential-helper trade-off is a documentation item, not a blocker. (I can't run the suite from the cron sandbox — the green CI run stands on its own.)

events.body:
Thanks for the review. I addressed the follow-up items in `e7595b8`:

- Force `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` in `_clean_git_env()` instead of merely scrubbing an inherited value, so HTTPS auth failures fail fast rather than waiting on an interactive prompt.
- Extended the env-hardening regression test to assert inherited `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1` is overridden to `0` while preserving `GIT_INDEX_FILE`.
- Updated `docs/workspace-git.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the PR body to explicitly cover `core.askPass=`, `credential.helper=`, `GIT_ASKPASS`/`SSH_ASKPASS`, and the private-HTTPS credential-helper trade-off.

Validation:
- `python -m pytest tests/test_workspace_git.py -q` → 43 passed
- `python -m ruff check api/workspace_git.py tests/test_workspace_git.py` → All checks passed
- GitHub checks are green on the updated head.

Confirmed `e7595b8` read-only against the PR HEAD — the follow-ups land correctly.

## `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is forced, not scrubbed

The placement is exactly right. The assignment runs *after* the `extra` merge and *after* both scrub loops, so it overrides an inherited value, a scrubbed-then-absent value, and anything a caller passes via `extra`:

```python
# api/workspace_git.py:72-82
def _clean_git_env(extra: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    env = os.environ.copy()
    if extra:
        env.update(extra)
    for key in _GIT_ENV_SCRUB_KEYS:
        env.pop(key, None)
    for key in list(env):
        if key.startswith(_GIT_ENV_SCRUB_PREFIXES):
            env.pop(key, None)
    env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
    return env
```

This is the fail-fast behavior I was after: with `credential.helper=""` and `core.askPass=""` disabled, a private-HTTPS 401 now returns an immediate auth error instead of blocking on a terminal prompt until `GIT_REMOTE_TIMEOUT` (60s) expires while holding the mutation lock.

## Test asserts the override, not just absence

The regression extension is the correct shape — it seeds an inherited `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1` and asserts it's forced to `0`, while still proving `GIT_INDEX_FILE` survives:

```python
# tests/test_workspace_git.py:1081,1097
monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT", "1")
...
assert env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] == "0"
assert env["GIT_INDEX_FILE"] == "/tmp/hermes-index"
```

That distinguishes "forced" from "merely scrubbed," which was the subtlety worth pinning down.

All three of my pre-merge asks are addressed: the `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` *set*, the doc/CHANGELOG sync covering `core.askPass=`/`credential.helper=` and the private-HTTPS trade-off, and the body update. No remaining blockers from my side. (Per cron policy I can't run the suite here — the green CI on the updated head plus your local `43 passed` / clean ruff stand on their own.)

events.body:
Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes a bug where a stale `_index.json` could hide pre-compression snapshots that contain more transcript rows than their continuation, causing messages to appear lost in the sidebar. It also stitches snapshot parents into the full transcript when a compression continuation is opened. - **Stale snapshot detection** (`api/models.py`): introduces `_stale_snapshot_metadata_refresh_ids`, which stat()s candidate snapshot sidecars when their indexed count does not already beat the visible continuation, and refreshes only those whose sidecar mtime is newer than the indexed content timestamp. `_prefer_fuller_snapshots_for_sidebar` is updated to show *both* rows (snapshot and continuation) when recency and completeness disagree, so no reachable message is hidden. - **Full transcript stitching** (`api/routes.py`): adds `_webui_sidecar_lineage_messages_for_display`, which walks the `pre_compression_snapshot` parent chain (up to 20 hops, with cycle detection) and merges messages oldest-to-newest so opening a compression child exposes the archived parent transcript. - **Tests** (`tests/`): four new tests cover the stale-index fix, the truthful-index non-regression, orphan snapshot exclusion, and the split-lineage double-visibility behaviour.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge; the targeted stat/refresh path is well-bounded by the indexed-count pre-check, and three dedicated regression tests confirm both the fix and its non-regression on the truthful-index path. The stale snapshot detection correctly gates sidecar reads behind an indexed-count comparison that filters the majority of candidates before touching the filesystem. The new message-stitching function in routes.py includes cycle detection and a hop limit, and is verified by tests that cover both the compression-parent stitch and the must-not-stitch fork case. No correctness defects were found in the changed code paths. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | api/models.py | Core logic change: targeted sidecar stat/refresh via _stale_snapshot_metadata_refresh_ids and updated _prefer_fuller_snapshots_for_sidebar; the 0.001s mtime epsilon may not filter reliably in production but is not a correctness bug. | | api/routes.py | New _webui_sidecar_lineage_messages_for_display correctly stitches pre_compression_snapshot parents with cycle detection and hop limit; all call sites updated consistently. | | tests/test_session_index.py | Three new regression tests verify the stale-index bug fix, the truthful-index non-regression (asserting load_metadata_only is never called), and orphan snapshot exclusion; existing newer-continuation test updated for the intentional double-row behaviour. | | tests/test_session_lineage_full_transcript.py | Two new tests verify WebUI compression child stitches parent transcript on GET /api/session, and that a normal fork does not incorrectly stitch its parent. | | tests/test_session_import_cli_fallback_model.py | One-line source-assertion update to match the renamed sidecar_messages assignment; no logic change. | | CHANGELOG.md | Changelog entry added for the stale-index sidebar bug fix. |

Flowchart

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[all_sessions poll] --> B[_refresh_index_rows_from_sidecar_metadata] B --> C[_stale_snapshot_metadata_refresh_ids] C --> D{For each lineage group\nwith visible + snapshot rows} D --> E{snapshot indexed count\n> visible count?} E -- Yes --> F[Skip — index is truthful] E -- No --> G[stat sidecar mtime] G --> H{mtime > indexed_ts\n+ 0.001s?} H -- No --> F H -- Yes --> I[Add to stale_snapshot_ids] I --> J[Session.load_metadata_only\nrefresh row] J --> K[_prefer_fuller_snapshots_for_sidebar] K --> L{refreshed count\n> visible count?} L -- No --> M[Keep snapshot hidden] L -- Yes --> N{continuation newer\nthan snapshot?} N -- No --> O[Show snapshot\nHide continuation] N -- Yes --> P[Show BOTH rows\nsplit-lineage display] Q[GET /api/session] --> R[_webui_sidecar_lineage_messages_for_display] R --> S{parent_session_id\nexists + is snapshot?} S -- No --> T[Return session.messages] S -- Yes --> U[Session.load parent\nappend to segments] U --> S U --> V[Merge oldest→newest\nacross all segments] V --> W[Return stitched transcript] ```

events.message: Fix sidebar visibility for stale compression snapshots

events.body:
## Summary

Reviewed read-only against `origin/master`: the diff for `api/models.py` + `api/routes.py`, the full pre/post versions of `_prefer_fuller_snapshots_for_sidebar` and `_row_may_need_sidecar_metadata_refresh`, and the two new `test_session_index.py` cases. CI is green across all 11 checks. The core fix is correct and the stat-gating is the right instinct. Two notes — one on a new per-poll `stat()`, one on the open-path `Session.load` cost — plus how this lines up with #3740.

## The visibility fix is correct

On `origin/master`, `_prefer_fuller_snapshots_for_sidebar` bails the moment the continuation is newer, even when the snapshot is the fuller transcript — which is exactly the "messages look lost" symptom:

```python
# api/models.py (master) — fuller snapshot stays hidden if continuation is newer
if newest_visible_ts > snapshot_ts:
    continue
snapshot_ids_to_show.add(str(best_snapshot.get('session_id')))
```

The PR inverts the order: the snapshot is added to `snapshot_ids_to_show` *first*, then the newer-continuation branch only skips *hiding the continuation* rather than skipping the whole snapshot. Showing both rows for a split lineage is the safe call — every reachable message stays visible. Agreed with the "tidy and wrong is how users start doubting reality" comment.

## The stale-index path — gating is good, the `stat()` is new per-poll work

`_stale_snapshot_metadata_refresh_ids` only stats a sidecar when a hidden snapshot's *indexed* count is ≤ the visible continuation and the sidecar mtime is newer than the indexed timestamp:

```python
# api/models.py (PR HEAD)
if _sidebar_message_count(snapshot) > best_visible_count:
    continue
if _sidecar_mtime_after_index_timestamp(snapshot):
    refresh_ids.add(sid)
```

This is well-scoped — it won't stat normal older snapshots. But note `_stale_snapshot_metadata_refresh_ids` now runs the full lineage-grouping pass (`_sidebar_lineage_root_id` over every session) on **every** `/api/sessions` poll, before the existing `_prefer_fuller_snapshots_for_sidebar` grouping does the same walk again. On a large sidebar that's two O(N·depth) lineage walks per poll where master did one. Probably fine, but worth a comment noting it, or memoizing the `groups`/`sessions_by_id` build so both consumers share it.

## Open-path concern: `Session.load` per parent hop, uncached

`_webui_sidecar_lineage_messages_for_display` (`routes.py:2869`) walks up to `max_hops=20` parents calling `Session.load(parent_id)` each:

```python
# api/routes.py (PR HEAD)
parent = Session.load(parent_id)
if not parent or not getattr(parent, "pre_compression_snapshot", False):
    break
segments.append(parent)
```

Two things: (1) the loop correctly stops at the first non-`pre_compression_snapshot` parent, so ordinary forks aren't stitched — good, that matches the docstring. (2) But this is now called from **both** `_merged_session_messages_for_display` and the `else` branch at `routes.py:5402` for every `GET /api/session`. For a deeply compressed lineage that's up to 20 sidecar reads + N `merge_session_messages_append_only` passes synchronously on the request path. If `Session.load` isn't already memoized within a request, a deep chain could add real latency to session open. Worth confirming the load is cheap/cached, or capping more aggressively than 20.

## Relationship to #3740

This is the snapshot-lineage sibling of #3740 (stale `message_count: 0` hiding a messageful session). #3740 is the general "index says 0, disk says N" case; this PR fixes the narrower "snapshot indexed as shorter than it really is, so the fuller transcript stays hidden." The `_sidecar_mtime_after_index_timestamp` gate here is a good pattern that #3740's broader fix could reuse. Might be worth cross-linking so they don't diverge on how they detect index staleness.

## Verdict

Correct fix for a real "messages look lost" bug, tests assert the behavior directly (both the refresh and the no-refresh-when-truthful case), no auth/routing/data-model paths touched. Not a blocker, but I'd want: a note on the double lineage-walk per poll, and confirmation that the open-path `Session.load` chain is cheap before merge. (I can't run the suite from the cron sandbox — the green CI and your local `91 passed` stand on their own.)

Merged into master via release **v0.51.311** (Release KA, brick-wave) in #3776 — rebased cleanly onto fresh master, changed lines verified byte-identical to this PR head. Full suite green (8176 passed), Codex SAFE-TO-SHIP, Opus SHIP-IT (verified the stat() bound + snapshot-vs-fork lineage walk). Thanks @ai-ag2026! 🙏

## Release v0.51.311 — Release KA (brick-wave)

Batches two independent, high-severity contributor fixes. Both rebased cleanly onto fresh `origin/master` (behind=0), changed lines verified byte-identical to the PR heads.

### Security — workspace Git config RCE hardening (#3769, @Hinotoi-agent)
A malicious or restored workspace repository could turn read-only `git status` / default-enabled `git fetch --prune` into host command execution via repo-local executable config (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.askPass`, `credential.helper`, `protocol.ext.allow=always`). All workspace Git subprocesses now pass hardened `-c` overrides that ignore that repo-local executable config, scrub inherited `GIT_ASKPASS`/`SSH_ASKPASS`/`GIT_SSH`/`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, and set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so private HTTPS remotes fail fast. Also neutralizes `core.gitProxy` (folded in from the Opus pre-release review — residual `git://`-fetch proxy-command vector).

### Fixed — stale-snapshot sidebar visibility (#3770, @ai-ag2026)
After compaction, the sidebar could hide the archived pre-compression snapshot row when `_index.json` was stale (snapshot's on-disk sidecar had MORE transcript rows than the indexed count), making a conversation look like it lost messages. Snapshot rows now refresh their sidecar metadata before the lineage visibility decision, and `GET /api/session` stitches the archived snapshot parent into the merged display transcript.

## Gate (all green)
- **Full suite:** 8176 passed, 9 skipped, 2 xfailed, 1 xpassed, 0 failed (318s, `-p no:xdist`)
- **Codex regression gate:** SAFE TO SHIP — no regression risk; core flows intact
- **Opus advisor:** SHIP IT — both PRs correct, well-tested; one SHOULD-FIX (`core.gitProxy`) folded in
- Ruff forward gate clean · revert-guard PASS (origin/master is ancestor of HEAD) · py-syntax/merge-marker/CHANGELOG checks clean

## Follow-up (not blocking)
Destructive-path Git config defense-in-depth (`core.hooksPath`, `filter.*`, `gpg.program` — gated behind `HERMES_WEBUI_WORKSPACE_GIT_DESTRUCTIVE=1` opt-in) to be filed as a separate hardening issue.

Four integration tests exercise each RCE vector with real subprocess Git calls. - **`api/models.py` + `api/routes.py`**: `_prefer_fuller_snapshots_for_sidebar` now unconditionally exposes a fuller snapshot (previously gated on recency), showing both snapshot and continuation when they disagree on which is fuller vs. newer. `_stale_snapshot_metadata_refresh_ids` + `_sidecar_mtime_after_index_timestamp` detect sidecars that grew after the index was written and trigger a targeted re-read. `_webui_sidecar_lineage_messages_for_display` stitches `pre_compression_snapshot` parent chains into `GET /api/session` so archived turns are visible when opening a compression child.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 Safe to merge. Both fixes address real, well-described bugs with solid integration-test backing. No regressions identified in the changed paths. The git hardening is thorough and backed by four live subprocess tests that verify each blocked vector. The stale-snapshot fix correctly moves the snapshot_ids_to_show.add call before the recency guard, and the sidecar refresh path is scoped to avoid scanning every historical row on each poll. The main gap is that _sidecar_mtime_after_index_timestamp's comparison logic is never exercised in a scenario where it should return False — the tests use synthetic timestamps (100–301 s) that guarantee OS mtime >> indexed_ts, so a regression that broke the comparison direction would not be caught by those tests. Additionally, core.sshCommand=ssh silently overrides repo-local SSH key selection, which the docs don't fully describe for the SSH case. pull_list.title: Fix heap OOB read in VLAN decapsulation memmove
pull_list.body:
## Summary

In `lldpd_decode()`, the VLAN decapsulation `memmove` shifts frame data 4 bytes left starting at offset `2*ETHER_ADDR_LEN`. The source pointer is correctly offset by +4, but the length argument uses the full remaining frame length (`s - 2*ETHER_ADDR_LEN`) instead of accounting for the 4-byte shift (`s - 2*ETHER_ADDR_LEN - 4`).

When the received frame fills the hardware MTU allocation exactly, the `memmove` source range extends 4 bytes past the end of the heap buffer.

## Fix

Subtract the 4-byte VLAN tag size from the `memmove` length, matching the source offset adjustment.

description: lldpd is an implementation of IEEE 802.1ab (LLDP). Prior to version 1.0.22, lldpd_decode() in src/daemon/lldpd.c strips 802.1Q VLAN tags from received Ethernet frames by calling memmove() to shift the frame payload 4 bytes left. The third argument (byte count) is s - 2 * ETHER_ADDR_LEN but should be s - 2 * ETHER_ADDR_LEN - 4, causing a 4-byte heap buffer over-read past the malloc(h_mtu) allocation when the received frame size equals the interface MTU. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.22.

description: Pipecat is an open-source Python framework for building real-time voice and multimodal conversational agents. From version 0.0.90 to before version 1.2.0, a path traversal vulnerability exists in Pipecat's development runner (src/pipecat/runner/run.py). When the runner is started with the --folder flag, it exposes a GET /files/{filename:path} download endpoint. The filename path parameter is concatenated directly onto args.folder with no containment check. Starlette normalises literal ../ sequences in URLs, but %2F-encoded slashes bypass this normalisation: the path parameter is URL-decoded after routing, so ..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd resolves to a path two levels above args.folder. An attacker with network access to the runner can read any file the pipecat process has permission to access — including SSH private keys, credentials, and system files — with a single unauthenticated HTTP request. This issue has been patched in version 1.2.0.

issue_list.title: Onboarding OAuth start: make single-flight atomic under concurrent starts (follow-up to #3970)
issue_list.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from #3970 (onboarding OAuth single-flight). The single-flight guard added there fixes the reported *sequential* vector but is not atomic under **concurrent** starts.

## The race

`api/oauth.py::_pending_oauth_flow_for(provider, hermes_home)` acquires `_OAUTH_FLOWS_LOCK`, checks for a live pending flow, then **releases the lock**. The caller then does the device-code request and inserts the new flow. So:

```
check (lock held) → release → request device code → insert flow → spawn worker
```

Two simultaneous unauthenticated `POST /api/onboarding/oauth/start` requests for the same provider/home can both pass the existence check before either inserts → both request device codes, both spawn polling workers, both leave pending flows. Codex reproduced this with a concurrent two-thread start against the #3970 head.

- **Codex path** (`start_onboarding_oauth_flow`, oauth.py:~749): larger window (includes the `_request_codex_user_code()` network round-trip).
- **Anthropic path** (`_start_anthropic_flow`, oauth.py:~705): same shape, smaller window.

## Severity

Low. #3970 already reduces accumulation from O(total requests) → O(burst-concurrency within one ~15-min flow lifetime), the reported 25-requests→25-workers vector is fully fixed, and the 300s terminal purge cleans stragglers. This is a tightening of the guard's stated "single-flight" contract under concurrency, not a re-opening of the original DoS.

## Fix

Make **check → reserve → spawn** atomic per `(canonical_provider, canonical_hermes_home)`:

- A per-key start lock (`dict[key, threading.Lock]` guarded by a meta-lock, or a single coarse start lock) held across the existence check, device-code request, flow insertion, and worker spawn; or
- Insert a placeholder `pending` flow under the **same** `_OAUTH_FLOWS_LOCK` acquisition as the existence check (before the device-code request), rolling it back on failure.

Add a regression test driving two concurrent starts for the same provider/home, asserting exactly one worker spawn / one `flow_id`.

Refs #3970.
